The inter-universal Teichm¨uller theory developed in [IUTchI], [IUTchII], [IUTchIII],
[IUTchIV] arose from attempts by the author, which began around the summer of
2000, to overcome certain technical obstructions in the scheme-theoretic Hodge-
Arakelov theory of [HASurI], [HASurII] to applying this theory to diophantine geom-
etry [cf. the discussion of [HASurI], §1.5.1; [HASurII], Remark 3.7; [IUTchI], Remark
4.3.1]. Thus, we begin our overview of inter-universal Teichm¨uller theory with a brief
review of the essential content of those aspects of scheme-theoretic Hodge-Arakelov
theory that are relevant to the development of inter-universal Teichm¨uller theory.
Let l be a prime number. Then we recall that the module E[l] of l-torsion points
of a Tate curve E def
= Gm/qZ [over, say, a p-adic field or the complex field C], whose
q-parameter we denote by q, fits into a natural exact sequence
0 −→ μl −→ E[l] −→ Z/lZ −→ 0.
That is to say, one has canonical objects as follows:
a “multiplicative subspace” μl ⊆ E[l] and “generators” ±1 ∈ Z/lZ.
In the following discussion, we fix an elliptic curve E over a number field F
and a prime number l ≥ 5. For convenience, we shall use the notation
l def
= l−1
2 .
Also, we suppose that E has stable reduction at all nonarchimedean primes of F . Then,
in general, the module E[l] [i.e., more precisely, the finite ´etale group scheme over F ] of
l-torsion points of E does not admit
a “global multiplicative subspace” or “global canonical generators”
— i.e., a rank one submodule M ⊆ E[l] or a pair of generators of the quotient E[l]/M
that coincide with the above canonical multiplicative subspace and generators at all
nonarchimedean primes of F where E has bad multiplicative reduction. Nevertheless,
let us
suppose that such global objects do in fact exist
Also, let us write
K def
= F (E[l])
for the extension field of F generated by the fields of definition of the l-torsion points
of E, V(K) for the set of [archimedean and nonarchimedean] valuations of K, and
A Panoramic Overview of Inter-universal Teichm¨uller Theory 3
V(K)bad ⊆ V(K) for the set of nonarchimedean valuations where E has bad multiplica-
tive reduction. For v ∈ V(K), we shall write Kv for the completion of K at v, Ov ⊆ Kv
for the subset of elements f ∈ Kv such that |f |v ≤ 1, and mv ⊆ Ov for the subset of
elements f ∈ Kv such that |f |v < 1. Let N ⊆ E[l] be a rank one submodule such that
the natural morphism of finite group schemes over F
M × N ∼
→ E[l]
is an isomorphism. Then the Fundamental Theorem of Hodge-Arakelov Theory may be
formulated as follows [cf. [HASurI], §1; [HASurII], §1, §3; the explicit series representa-
tion of the theta function on a Tate curve given in [EtTh], Proposition 1.4]

phase_0.boundary_condition: The log-theta-lattice containing all inter-universal deformations

VINIT.justification: The initial numerical seed before the construction of the Tate curve or Hodge theater.

TANCH.chosen_element: The Fundamental Theorem of Hodge-Arakelov Theory
TANCH.justification: The terminal bounding result that constrains the entire arithmetic deformation space.

AFWD.justification: The forward expansion of the base field to include all l-torsion point definitions.

AREV.justification: The descent from abstract group schemes to specific local valuation behaviors.

CLINK.chosen_element: M x N isomorphism to E[l]
CLINK.justification: The composition of multiplicative and canonical submodules to reconstruct the full torsion module.

IMSCRIB.justification: The self-recognition of the arithmetic fundamental group across different theaters.

FSPLIT.justification: The branching of the l-torsion module into the multiplicative subspace and the quotient generators.

FFUSE.justification: The reunification of the multiplicative subspace and quotient to recover the original torsion scheme.

EVALT.justification: The affirmative state where local canonical objects align into a global structure.

EVALF.justification: The failure state where technical barriers prevent direct application to diophantine geometry.

ENGAGR.justification: The simultaneous holding of distinct arithmetic topoi that are non-isomorphic yet linked.

IFIX.justification: The permanent, fixed record of all archimedean and nonarchimedean valuations.

phase_3.void_description: Pre-arithmetic state before the selection of prime l and elliptic curve E
phase_3.true_description: Successful global synchronization of multiplicative subspaces across all valuations
phase_3.false_description: Local-global incompatibility of canonical generators at bad reduction primes
phase_3.both_description: The log-theta-lattice state where multiple arithmetic versions coexist via the theta-link

steps.domain_action: Select prime l and elliptic curve E over number field F
Construct the Tate curve Gm/qZ and define the q-parameter
Branch E[l] into the multiplicative subspace mu_l and quotient Z/lZ
Identify canonical generators +/- 1 in the quotient
Reconstitute the torsion module structure E[l]
Record the set of valuations V(K) and identify V(K)bad
Map the local multiplicative subspaces to the global field extension K
Test for the existence of a global rank one submodule M
Encounter technical obstructions in standard scheme-theoretic Hodge-Arakelov theory
Revert to local completions Kv and rings of integers Ov to analyze bad reduction
Invoke inter-universal theaters to hold conflicting arithmetic structures simultaneously
Establish mono-anabelian self-reference to maintain identity across theaters
Resolve the global object existence through the theta-link deformation
Finalize the series representation of the theta function as the system boundary

phase_5.compiler_frontend: The Frobenioids and Etale Theta Functions
phase_5.memory_mechanism: The universe of all valuations V(K)
phase_5.scheduler_mechanism: The sequence of IUTch papers I through IV

phase_6.delta_s_verdict: ΔS ≈ 0 — The information content of the arithmetic fundamental group is preserved via mono-anabelian geometry.
